The Dakotas were the last great farming frontier.
The boom of 1878 to 87 had filled the eastern counties along the railroads; after 1900 a second rush opened the West
River country beyond the Missouri, and in 1907 the railroads reached Rapid City.
The Wintrode sons went with it. Harry Wintrode, born in Illinois and raised in Ida County,
was on the Turner County jury list at Parker by 1905, the year he married Elizabeth Fritz of Black Hawk County,
whose parents and grandmother Catharine also ended their days at Parker, where her mother’s brothers Joseph and Edward
Staebell had settled too. His brother William farmed near Parker and later ranched on Box Elder Creek near Rapid City;
Edward, Clarence and Frank took up land around Philip, in the new West River country.
Their widowed father spent his last years among them and died at William’s ranch in 1922.
It was hard country: drought, hail, grasshoppers, and the dust years of the 1930s.
Harry died in 1933. His son Maurice, born at Parker in 1923, grew up there.
